agent.runner_summary: Runs the Jataayu injection-triage agent through a thin OpenAI Agents SDK simulator adapter that accepts one raw string per turn.

components.when_to_use: Use component environments when you want to isolate the direct guard-tool verdict instead of evaluating the full LLM triage response.
components.input_guidance: Pass JSON kwargs matching the tool schema: required `content` string and optional `surface` string such as `tool-return` or `github-issue`.
components.output_guidance: Expect a JSON string containing `status`, `score`, and `findings`; evaluate whether the guard classified the supplied content as expected.

log_notes: Agent environments should provide FixedTurn content as a raw string, not a JSON wrapper object.
Successful full-agent outputs are intended to be a single line beginning with `BLOCK:` or `ALLOW:` because that is the agent instruction contract.
Transcript mock-call entries appear only when a learning environment mocks `jataayu_guard_agent.agent:jataayu_scan`.
learning_env_guidance: For agent environments, set each FixedTurn content value to the exact untrusted text snippet the agent should triage.
Prefer short standalone snippets from surfaces like retrieved content, email, issue text, or tool returns; the adapter wraps the string into a single user message internally.
Use `jataayu_guard_agent.agent:jataayu_scan` as the component target for direct tool tests, with named kwargs instead of positional args.
Leave `jataayu_guard_agent.agent:jataayu_scan` live by default for end-to-end guard behavior, but mock it when a scenario specifically needs a fixed tool verdict.
Prefer OpenAI when `OPENAI_API_KEY` is available; otherwise set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and expect the agent to run through LiteLLM with the configured Anthropic default model.
